questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Expedite, Hasten, Hurry, __________
Fill the blank by choosing a word with a meaning similar to that of the words
given above.
questions.explanationEn: 'Expedite', 'Hasten', and 'Hurry' are all synonyms meaning to speed up or cause something to happen sooner. 'Accelerate' shares this exact meaning, whereas 'Retard', 'Provide', and 'Disable' do not.

Panel I. Which one of the shapes in Panel II is the other part?
questions.explanationEn: Matching the complementary edge profile and corner geometry needed to complete square PQRS from the piece in Panel I identifies shape (iii) in Panel II (Option C; refer to the official figures).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
A day can only be cloudy or sunny. The probability of a day being cloudy is 0.5,
independent of the condition on other days. What is the probability that in any
given four days, there will be three cloudy days and one sunny day?
questions.explanationEn: Each day is independently cloudy with p = 0.5. By the binomial distribution, the probability of 3 cloudy days and 1 sunny day in 4 days is C(4, 3) * (0.5)^3 * (0.5)^1 = 4 / 16 = 1/4.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
The values of Stock A and Stock B on a particular day are Rs. 50 and Rs. 80,
respectively. An investor invests Rs. 100 in Stock A and Rs. 80 in Stock B. He
sells all the stocks the next day when the value of Stock A is Rs. 55 and Stock B
is Rs. 70. The profit made by the investor is Rs. ________
questions.explanationEn: The investor buys 100/50 = 2 shares of Stock A and 80/80 = 1 share of Stock B (total investment Rs. 180). The next day, selling them yields 2*55 + 1*70 = 110 + 70 = Rs. 180, so the profit is 180 - 180 = Rs. 0.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
‘When it is raining, peacocks dance.’
Based only on this sentence, which one of the following options is necessarily
true?
optionsEn: Peacocks dance only when it is raining.
When peacocks dance, it is raining.
When peacocks are not dancing, it is not raining.
When it is not raining, peacocks do not dance.
questions.explanationEn: The statement 'When it is raining (R), peacocks dance (D)' is the implication R -> D. Its logically equivalent contrapositive is not D -> not R: 'When peacocks are not dancing, it is not raining' (Option C).

Water : P :: Food : Q
Choose the P and Q combination from the options below to form a meaningful
analogy.
questions.explanationEn: Water satisfies/relieves thirst, just as food satisfies/relieves hunger. Thus P = Thirst and Q = Hunger completes the analogy.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Figures (i) and (ii) represent intercity highway systems. The black dots represent
cities and the line segments between them represent intercity highways.
A salesperson needs to make a trip. She needs to start from a city, visit each of the
remaining cities exactly once, and finally return to the same city from which she
started.
Which one of the following options is then true?
optionsEn: Such a trip is possible for (i), but not for (ii).
Such a trip is possible for (ii), but not for (i).
Such a trip is possible for both (i) and (ii).
Such a trip is possible neither for (i) nor for (ii).
questions.explanationEn: The required trip is a Hamiltonian cycle (visiting every vertex once and returning to start). Inspecting the two highway graphs shows graph (i) contains a Hamiltonian cycle while graph (ii) has a cut vertex/degree-1 bottleneck preventing one (Option A; refer to the official diagram).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
An unbiased six-faced dice whose faces are marked with numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5,
and 6 is rolled twice in succession and the number on the top face is recorded
each time. The probability that the sum of the two recorded numbers is a prime
number is ________
questions.explanationEn: Two dice give 36 equally likely sums from 2 to 12. The prime sums are 2 (1 way), 3 (2 ways), 5 (4 ways), 7 (6 ways), and 11 (2 ways), totaling 1 + 2 + 4 + 6 + 2 = 15 favorable outcomes, so probability = 15/36.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
For two different persons x and y, the predicate M(x, y) denotes that x knows y.
Consider the following statement.
There is a person who does not know anyone else, but that person is known by
everyone else.
Which one of the following expressions represents the above statement?
questions.explanationEn: 'There is a person y' uses (exists y), and 'every other person x (x != y) knows y and y does not know x' translates to (forall x)((x != y) -> (M(x, y) and not M(y, x))), matching Option (A).

Which one of the following statements is equivalent to the following assertion?

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn: In C runtime environment, which one of the following is stored in heap?
optionsEn: A static variable declared inside a function
An array of integers declared inside a function
A dynamically allocated array of integers created using malloc() function call
questions.explanationEn: In a C runtime environment, dynamically allocated memory via malloc()/calloc() resides on the heap (C). Static variables live in the data/BSS segment, and local arrays and return addresses live on the call stack.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following two statements about interrupt handling mechanisms in a
CPU.
S1: In non-vectored interrupt mechanism, it usually takes more time to start the
Interrupt Service Routine (ISR) when compared to that in a vectored interrupt
mechanism.
S2: In daisy-chain interrupt mechanism, the CPU polls all the input devices
individually to determine the source of the interrupt.
Which one of the following options is correct with respect to S1 and S2 ?
optionsEn: Both S1 and S2 are true
Both S1 and S2 are false
S1 is true and S2 is false
S1 is false and S2 is true
questions.explanationEn: In non-vectored interrupts, the CPU jumps to a fixed handler and polls devices to identify the interrupter, taking longer to start the specific ISR than vectored interrupts (S1 true). In daisy-chain interrupts, the interrupt acknowledge signal propagates down the hardware chain so the CPU does NOT poll every device individually (S2 false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider concurrent execution of two transactions T1 and T2 in a DBMS, both of
which access a data object A. For these two transactions to not conflict on A, which
one of the following statements must be true?
optionsEn: Both T1 and T2 only read A
T1 reads A and T2 writes A
T1 writes A and T2 reads A
Both T1 and T2 write A
questions.explanationEn: Two operations on the same data item A conflict if at least one of them is a write (RW, WR, or WW). Therefore, T1 and T2 do not conflict on A only if both transactions only read A (Option A).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a file of size 4 million bytes being transferred between two hosts
connected via a path consisting of three consecutive links of bandwidth 2 Mbps,
500 kbps, and 1 Mbps, respectively. All processing delays and propagation delays
are negligible. Assume that there is no other background traffic over the path and
no other additional overhead to transfer the file.
Which one of the following is the total time (in seconds) to transfer the file?
Note: 1M=106, 1k=103
questions.explanationEn: The bottleneck link bandwidth along the path is min(2 Mbps, 500 kbps, 1 Mbps) = 500 kbps = 500 * 10^3 bits/sec. File size = 4 * 10^6 bytes = 32 * 10^6 bits. With negligible propagation/processing delays, transfer time = (32 * 10^6) / (500 * 10^3) = 64 seconds.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following protocols may need to broadcast some of its messages?
questions.explanationEn: DHCP clients do not initially have an IP address or know the DHCP server's address, so they broadcast DHCPDISCOVER (and DHCPREQUEST) packets across the local subnet. SMTP, FTP, and HTTP operate over unicast TCP connections.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following CPU scheduling algorithms cannot be preemptive?
questions.explanationEn: First Come First Serve (FCFS) strictly runs processes in arrival order to completion (or I/O block) and is inherently non-preemptive. SRTF and Round Robin are preemptive by definition, and Priority Scheduling can be preemptive.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following functions, where n is a positive integer.
n1/3 , log(n) , log(n!), 2log(n)
Which one of the following options lists the functions in increasing order of
asymptotic growth rate?
Note: Assume the base of log to be 2.
questions.explanationEn: Notice 2^(log2 n) = n, and by Stirling's approximation log(n!) = Theta(n log n). Comparing asymptotic growth: log(n) << n^(1/3) << n = 2^(log n) << n log n = Theta(log(n!)), which matches Option (A).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper

with time complexity Θ(n)?
questions.explanationEn: Solving T(n) = T(n-1) + 1 gives T(n) = n = Theta(n) (A). For T(n) = 2T(n/2) + 1, Master Theorem Case 1 gives Theta(n^(log_2 2)) = Theta(n) (B). Options (C) and (D) solve to Theta(n log n) and Theta(n^2), respectively.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let R be a binary relation on the set {1, 2, ... , 10}, where (x, y) ∈R if the product
of x and y is square of an integer. Which of the following properties is/are satisfied
by R?
questions.explanationEn: (x, y) in R iff xy is a perfect square. x*x = x^2 is always a square (Reflexive, A); xy = yx (Symmetric, B); if xy = a^2 and yz = b^2, then xz = (ab/y)^2 is a rational square of integers hence a perfect square (Transitive, C). Since (1, 4) and (4, 1) are both in R with 1 != 4, R is not antisymmetric.

optionsEn: The value of I(a) is independent of the value of a

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
In a system, numbers are represented using 4-bit two’s complement form. Consider
four numbers N1 =1011, N2 =1101, N3 =1010 and N4 =1001 in the system.
Which of the following operations will result in arithmetic overflow?
questions.explanationEn: In 4-bit 2's complement, the representable range is [-8, +7]. Here N1 = -5, N2 = -3, N3 = -6, N4 = -7. Checking operations: N1 + N2 = -8 (fits), N2 + N3 = -9 (overflow, B), N3 - N4 = +1 (fits), and N1 + N4 = -12 (overflow, D).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following grammars is/are ambiguous?
questions.explanationEn: E -> E + E | E * E | id is ambiguous due to lacking precedence/associativity (e.g., two parse trees for id + id * id, B). S -> aS | Sa | eps is ambiguous because 'a' can be generated as a(S) or (S)a (C). Grammars (A) and (D) are unambiguous.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
The keys 5, 28, 19, 15, 26, 33, 12, 17, 10 are inserted into a hash table using the
hash function h(k) = k mod 9. The collisions are resolved by chaining. After all
the keys are inserted, the length of the longest chain is __________. (answer in
integer)
questions.explanationEn: Hashing with h(k) = k mod 9: 5->5, 28->1, 19->1, 15->6, 26->8, 33->6, 12->3, 17->8, 10->1. Bucket 1 holds {28, 19, 10} (length 3), bucket 6 holds {15, 33} (length 2), and bucket 8 holds {26, 17} (length 2), so the longest chain has length 3.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the system of linear equations given below.
ax+ y= b
16x+ ay= 24
Suppose the values of a and b are chosen such that the system of linear equations
produce multiple solutions. Then the product of a and b is __________. (answer in
integer)
questions.explanationEn: For ax + y = b and 16x + ay = 24 to have infinitely many (multiple) solutions, the coefficients must be proportional: a/16 = 1/a = b/24. From a^2 = 16 we get a = +/- 4, and from b = 24/a we get b = +/- 6 (with matching signs), so in both cases a*b = 24.

A merge operation on sorted left array L and sorted right array R is said to be void

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
If an IP network uses a subnet mask of 255.255.240.0, the maximum number of IP
addresses that can be assigned to network interfaces is __________. (answer in
integer)
questions.explanationEn: Subnet mask 255.255.240.0 has 12 host bits (32 - 20 = 12, since 240 = 11110000_2 leaves 4 bits in the 3rd octet + 8 bits in the 4th). Excluding the all-0s network address and all-1s broadcast address leaves 2^12 - 2 = 4096 - 2 = 4094 assignable IP addresses.

questions.questionTextEn:
A lexical analyzer uses the following token definitions
• letter→[A−Za−z]
• digit→[0 −9]
• id→letter (letter | digit)*
• number→digit+
• ws→(blank | tab | newline)+
For the string given below,
x1 23mm 78 y 7z zz5 14A 8H AaYcD
the number of tokens (excluding ws) that will be produced by the lexical analyzer
is __________. (answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: Applying longest-match tokenization (id starts with letter, number is digits+): 'x1' (id), '23' (num), 'mm' (id), '78' (num), 'y' (id), '7' (num), 'z' (id), 'zz5' (id), '14' (num), 'A' (id), '8' (num), 'H' (id), 'AaYcD' (id). Counting all tokens excluding whitespace gives 13 tokens.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a complete graph Kn with n vertices (n> 4). Note that multiple spanning
trees can be constructed over Kn. Each of these spanning trees is represented as a
set of edges. The Jaccard coefficient between any two sets is defined as the ratio of
the size of the intersection of the two sets to the size of the union of the two sets.
Which one of the following options gives the lowest possible value for the Jaccard
coefficient between any two spanning trees of Kn ?
questions.explanationEn: In K_n for n > 4, the maximum number of edge-disjoint spanning trees is floor(n/2) >= 2 (each using n - 1 edges, since C(n, 2) >= 2(n - 1) for n >= 4). Picking two edge-disjoint spanning trees T1 and T2 gives |T1 intersect T2| = 0, making the Jaccard coefficient 0.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let G be a weighted directed acyclic graph with m edges and n vertices. Given G
and a source vertex s in G, which one of the following options gives the worst case
time complexity of the fastest algorithm to find the lengths of shortest paths from s
to all vertices that are reachable from s in G?
questions.explanationEn: In a weighted DAG, single-source shortest paths can be computed in Theta(m + n) worst-case time by topologically sorting the vertices in Theta(m + n) and relaxing outgoing edges once in topological order.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider an array A of integers of size n. The indices of A run from 1 to n. An
algorithm is to be designed to check whether A satisfies the condition given below.
∀i, j∈{1, ... , n−1} such that i> j, (A[i+ 1] −A[i]) > (A[j+ 1] −A[j])
Which one of the following gives the worst case time complexity of the fastest
algorithm that can be designed for the problem?
questions.explanationEn: The condition states that consecutive differences d[i] = A[i+1] - A[i] are strictly increasing (d[1] < d[2] < ... < d[n-1]). Checking d[i] < d[i+1] in a single linear scan takes Theta(n) time, and reading all n elements is necessary in the worst case, so Theta(n) is optimal.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a table T, where the elements T[i][j], 0 ≤i, j≤n, represent the cost of
the optimal solutions of different subproblems of a problem that is being solved
using a dynamic programming algorithm. The recursive formulation to compute the
table entries is as follows:
T[0][k] = T[k][0] = 1 for k= 0,1,2, ... , n
T[i][j] = 2T[i−1][j] + 3T[i][j−1] for 1 ≤i, j≤n
Consider the following two algorithms to compute entries of T. Assume that for
both the algorithms, for all 0 ≤i, j≤n, T[i][j] has been initialized to 1.
Algorithm B1: For i= 1, 2, ... , n
For j= 1, 2, ... , n
T[i][j] = 2T[i−1][j] + 3T[i][j−1]
Algorithm B2: For s= 2, 3, ... , 2n
For i= 1, 2, ... , n
For j= 1, 2, ... , n
If (i+ j== s)
T[i][j] = 2T[i−1][j] + 3T[i][j−1]
Algorithm Bk, k∈{1,2} is said to be correct if and only if it calculates the correct
values of T[i][j], for all 0 ≤i, j≤n, (as per the recursive formulation) at the end
of the execution of the algorithm Bk.
Which one of the following statements is true?
optionsEn: Both algorithms B1 and B2 are correct
Algorithm B1 is correct, but algorithm B2 is incorrect
Algorithm B2 is correct, but algorithm B1 is incorrect
Both algorithms B1 and B2 are incorrect
questions.explanationEn: T[i][j] depends only on T[i-1][j] (top neighbor) and T[i][j-1] (left neighbor). Algorithm B1 iterates row-by-row (top-to-bottom, left-to-right), and Algorithm B2 iterates along anti-diagonals i + j = s in increasing order; in both orders both dependencies are already computed, so both B1 and B2 are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following 4-variable Boolean function
F(A, B, C, D) = Σm(0, 1, 2, 3, 8, 9, 10, 11)
Consider A as MSB, D as LSB. Which one of the following options represents the
minimal sum of products form for the above function?
Note: + is OR operation, . is AND operation, ′ is NOT operation
questions.explanationEn: Minterms {0,1,2,3,8,9,10,11} correspond to all combinations where bit B = 0 (since 0..3 have AB=00 and 8..11 have AB=10, while C and D vary over all 4 combinations). Thus all 8 minterms combine into the single prime implicant B'.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the canonical LR(0) parsing of the grammar below using terminals
{a, b, c} and non-terminals {A, B, C, S} with S as the start symbol.
S→ACB
A→aA | ε
C→cC | ε
B→bB | b
Which one of the following options gives the number of shift-reduce conflicts that
will occur in the LR(0) ACTION table?
questions.explanationEn: Building the canonical LR(0) automaton for S' -> .S, S -> .ACB, A -> .aA | .eps, C -> .cC | .eps, B -> .bB | .b: any state containing a completed epsilon-reduction item [A -> .] or [C -> .] alongside shift items (e.g., shift 'a' vs reduce A -> eps in I0 and after 'a'; shift 'c' vs reduce C -> eps after A and after 'c'; plus shift 'b' vs reduce B -> b. in the state after 'b' where [B -> b.] and [B -> b.B] coexist) produces 5 states/actions with shift-reduce conflicts in the LR(0) table.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
In the context of schema normalization in relational DBMS, consider a set F of
functional dependencies. The set of all functional dependencies implied by F is
called the closure of F. To compute the closure of F, Armstrong’s Axioms can be
applied. Consider X, Y, and Z as sets of attributes over a relational schema. The three
rules of Armstrong’s Axioms are described as follows.
Reflexivity: If Y⊆X , then X→Y
Augmentation: If X→Y, then XZ→YZ for any Z
Transitivity: If X→Y and Y→Z, then X→Z
The additional rule of Union is defined as follows.
Union: If X→Y and X→Z, then X→YZ
It can be proved that the additional rule of Union is also implied by the three rules
of Armstrong’s Axioms. Listed below are four combinations of these three rules.
Which one of these combinations is both necessary and sufficient for the proof ?
questions.explanationEn: To prove Union (from X -> Y and X -> Z, derive X -> YZ): apply Augmentation to X -> Y using X to get X -> XY; apply Augmentation to X -> Z using Y to get XY -> YZ; then apply Transitivity to X -> XY and XY -> YZ to get X -> YZ. Reflexivity is not needed, so Augmentation and Transitivity are both necessary and sufficient.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the transmission of data bits 110001011 over a link that uses Cyclic
Redundancy Check (CRC) code for error detection. If the generator bit pattern is
given to be 1001, which one of the following options shows the remainder bit
pattern appended to the data bits before transmission?
questions.explanationEn: Generator 1001 has degree 3, so append three 0s to data 110001011 -> 110001011000. Performing modulo-2 polynomial division (XOR) by 1001 leaves the 3-bit remainder 100.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a processor that has 16 general purpose registers and it uses 2-byte
instruction format for all its instructions. Variable-sized opcodes are permitted.
There are three different types of instructions; M-type, R-type, and C-type. Each
M-type instruction has 2 register operands and a 6-bit immediate operand. Each R-
type instruction has 3 register operands. Each C-type instruction has a register
operand and a 6-bit offset value. If there are 2 unique M-type opcodes and 7 unique
R-type opcodes, which one of the following options gives the maximum number of
unique opcodes possible for C-type instructions?
questions.explanationEn: Each instruction is 16 bits and registers need 4 bits. M-type uses 2 regs + 6-bit imm = 14 bits (leaving 2-bit opcode prefixes: 2 out of 4 prefixes used, leaving 2 free 2-bit prefixes, i.e., 2 * 4 = 8 four-bit slots). R-type uses 3 regs = 12 bits (4-bit opcode: 7 out of those 8 slots used, leaving 1 four-bit prefix free). C-type uses 1 reg + 6-bit offset = 10 bits (6-bit opcode), and extending the remaining 1 four-bit prefix by 2 more bits yields 2^2 = 4 C-type opcodes.

Which one of the following options is the set of live variables at the exit point of

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
An index in a DBMS is said to be dense if an index entry appears for every
search-key value in the indexed file. Otherwise it is called a sparse index. Consider
the following two statements.
S1: A hash index must be a dense index
S2: A B+ tree index can be a sparse index
Which one of the following options is correct?
optionsEn: Both S1 and S2 are true
Both S1 and S2 are false
S1 is true and S2 is false
S1 is false and S2 is true
questions.explanationEn: A hash index hashes every search-key value to a bucket containing pointers to records, so it must have an entry for every search-key value (always dense, S1 true). In a B+ tree built on a sequentially ordered file, leaf entries can point only to the first record of each block (sparse index, S2 true).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following two finite automata D1 and D2.
Which of the following statements is/are true?
optionsEn: L(D1) is a proper subset of L(D2)
(L(D1) ∪L(D2)) ∗ consists of all strings in {0,1}∗ whose length is divisible by 3
questions.explanationEn: Inspecting automata D1 and D2 in the official figure shows their languages share only the empty string epsilon (L(D1) intersect L(D2) = {eps}, C), and taking (L(D1) union L(D2))* accepts exactly all strings over {0, 1}* whose length is a multiple of 3 (D).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let Σ = {a, b, c, d} and let L= {aibjckdl∣i, j, k, l≥0}.
Which of the following constraints ensure(s) that the language L is context-free?
questions.explanationEn: A PDA can push 'a's, match or adjust against 'b's, push 'c's, and pop against 'd's whenever the constraints pair adjacent or nested counters: i+k = j+l (A: push for a, pop for b, push/pop balance for c and d), i = l and j = k (C: push a's, push b's, pop b's with c's, pop a's with d's), and i+j = k+l (D: push for a and b, pop for c and d). Option (B) i=k and j=l is crossing-dependent (non-CFL).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a binary search tree (BST) with n leaf nodes (n> 0). Given any node V,
the key present in the node is denoted as Val(V). All the keys present in the given
BST are distinct. The keys belong to the set of real numbers.
For a node V, let Suc(V) denote the node that is its inorder successor. If a node V
does not have an inorder successor, then Suc(V) is NULL. As there are no
duplicates, if Suc(V) is not NULL, then Val(V) < Val(Suc(V)).
Corresponding to every leaf node Li that has a non-NULL Suc(Li), a new key ki
with the following property is to be inserted into the BST.
Val(Li) < ki< Val(Suc(Li))
Let K represent the list of all such new keys to be inserted into the BST.
Which of the following statements is/are true?
optionsEn: K will have at least one element
After inserting all keys from K, the height of the BST can increase at most by one
Number of nodes in the BST will double after inserting all keys from K
questions.explanationEn: Because Suc(Li) values are strictly increasing across leaves, the intervals (Val(Li), Val(Suc(Li))) are pairwise disjoint, so K has no duplicates (A). Each new key ki falls strictly between leaf Li and its inorder successor, so it is inserted either as the right child of Li or the leftmost child of Suc(Li) (only adding depth 1 below existing nodes without cascading), increasing the BST height by at most 1 (C). If n=1 (single root leaf), Suc is NULL so K can be empty (B false), and not all nodes are leaves (D false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a stack S and a queue Q. Both of them are initially empty and have the
capacity to store ten elements each. The elements 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 arrive one by one,
in that order. When an element arrives, it is assigned either to S (pushed on S ) or
to Q (enqueued to Q). Once all the five elements are stored, the output is generated
in two steps. First, stack S is emptied by popping all elements. Then queue Q is
emptied by dequeueing all elements. The output obtained by following this process
is 4 3 1 2 5 .
Given the output, the objective is to predict whether an element was assigned to S
or Q.
Which of the following options is/are possible valid assignment(s) of the
elements?
Note: In the options, the notation xS denotes that element x was assigned to S and
yQ denotes that element y was assigned to Q.
questions.explanationEn: Since S is emptied completely before Q, any prefix popped from S must be strictly decreasing in arrival order? No, wait: the output 4 3 1 2 5 has 4 3 decreasing (from S) followed by 1 2 5 increasing (from Q), OR 4 3 1 decreasing (from S) followed by 2 5 increasing (from Q). Note 1 cannot come from S after 3 unless 1 was pushed BEFORE 3 and 4, which gives 4, 3, 1 from S and 2, 5 from Q (Option A: 1S, 2Q, 3S, 4S, 5Q)! And if 1, 2, 5 were enqueued in Q and 3, 4 pushed to S, popping S gives 4, 3 and dequeuing Q gives 1, 2, 5 (Option B: 1Q, 2Q, 3S, 4S, 5Q). Options (C) and (D) cannot produce 4 3 1 2 5.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a system with a processor and a 4 KB direct mapped cache with block size
of 16 bytes. The system has a 16 MB physical memory. Four words P, Q, R, and S
are accessed by the processor in the same order 10 times. That is, there are a total
of 40 memory references in the sequence P, Q, R, S, P, Q, R, S,...
Assume that the cache memory is initially empty. The physical addresses of the
words are given below (1 word =1 byte).
P: 0x845B32, Q: 0x845B26, R: 0x845B36, S: 0x846B32
Which of the following statements is/are true?
Note: 1K=210 and 1M=220
optionsEn: Every access to P results in a cache miss
Every access to R results in a cache hit
Every access to Q results in a cache miss
Except the first access to S, all subsequent accesses to S result in cache hits
questions.explanationEn: With a 4 KB direct-mapped cache and 16-byte blocks, there are 256 blocks: bits [3:0] = offset (1 hex digit), bits [11:4] = index (2 hex digits), bits [23:12] = tag. Addresses: P=0x845B32 (tag 845, idx B3), Q=0x845B26 (tag 845, idx B2), R=0x845B36 (tag 845, idx B3), S=0x846B32 (tag 846, idx B3). P, R, and S all map to index B3: P (tag 845) misses every time because S (tag 846) evicts it at the end of every cycle (A), while R shares the exact same block (845, B3) loaded by P just before it and hits on every access (B).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
To keep track of free blocks in a file system, one of the two approaches is generally
used – using bitmaps (bit vectors) or using linked lists. Consider that the linked list
approach is used to keep track of free blocks in a file system. Assume that the disk
size is 16 GB, block size is 2 KB, and block numbers used are 32-bit long. A single
pointer of size 4 bytes is used in each block of the list to point to the next block of
the list. The number of blocks required to hold the free disk block numbers is
____________. (answer in integer)
Note: 1K=210 and 1G=230
questions.explanationEn: Total disk blocks = 16 GB / 2 KB = 2^34 / 2^11 = 2^23 = 8,388,608 blocks. Each 2 KB (2048-byte) list block uses 4 bytes for the next-block pointer, leaving 2044 bytes to store 2044 / 4 = 511 block numbers. Thus ceil(8,388,608 / 511) = ceil(16416.0626) = 16417 blocks are required.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
A system has a Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) that has a reach of 1 MB. TLB
reach is defined as the total amount of physical memory that can be accessed
through the TLB entries. The paging system uses pages of size 4 KB. The virtual
address space is 64 GB and physical address space is 1 GB. If each TLB entry stores
a 4-bit process id, page number, frame number, and a 2-bit control field, then the
size of the TLB (in bytes) is ___________. (answer in integer)
Note: 1K=210, 1M=220, 1G=230
questions.explanationEn: With 4 KB pages and 1 MB TLB reach, the TLB has 1 MB / 4 KB = 256 entries. For 64 GB (2^36 B) virtual and 1 GB (2^30 B) physical memory with 12-bit page offset, VPN = 24 bits and PFN = 18 bits. Each entry holds 4 (pid) + 24 (VPN) + 18 (PFN) + 2 (control) = 48 bits = 6 bytes, so TLB size = 256 * 6 = 1536 bytes.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider contiguous allocation of physical memory to processes using variable
partitioning scheme. Suppose there are 8 holes in the memory of sizes 20 KB, 4 KB,
25 KB, 18 KB, 7 KB, 9 KB, 15 KB, and 12 KB. Assume that no two holes are
adjacent. Two processes P1 of size 16 KB and P2 of size 9 KB arrive in that order,
and they are allocated memory using the best-fit technique. After allocating space
to P1 and P2, the number of holes of size less than 8 KB is ____________. (answer
in integer)
Note: 1K=210
questions.explanationEn: Initial holes: {20, 4, 25, 18, 7, 9, 15, 12}. P1 (16 KB) uses best-fit hole 18 KB, leaving a 2 KB hole: {20, 4, 25, 2, 7, 9, 15, 12}. P2 (9 KB) uses exact best-fit hole 9 KB, leaving 0 KB: {20, 4, 25, 2, 7, 15, 12}. The holes strictly smaller than 8 KB are 4 KB, 2 KB, and 7 KB—giving 3 holes.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a system with 1 MB physical memory and a word length of 1 byte. The
system uses a direct mapped cache, with block numbers starting from 0. The word
with physical address 0xA2C28 is mapped to the cache block number 17610. The
maximum possible size of the cache (in KB) for this configuration is ___________.
(answer in integer)
Note: 1K=210 and 1M=220
questions.explanationEn: Write 0xA2C28 in 20-bit binary: 1010 0010 1100 0010 1000. The cache block index 176_10 in binary is 10110000_2, which matches bits [13:6] of the address, with bits [16:14] = 000 above it (while bit 17 = 1). Extending the index up to bit 16 gives 11 index bits ([16:6]) and 6 block-offset bits ([5:0]), yielding maximum cache size 2^(11 + 6) = 2^17 bytes = 128 KB.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
A non-pipelined instruction execution unit that operates at 1.6 GHz clock takes an
average of 5 clock cycles to complete the execution of an instruction. To improve
the performance, the system was pipelined with a goal of achieving an average
throughput of one instruction per clock cycle. However, it could operate only at
1.2 GHz due to pipeline overheads. While executing a program in the pipelined
design, 30% of instructions encountered a stall of 2 cycles due to pipeline hazards.
The speed-up obtained by the pipelined design over the non-pipelined one for this
program is ___________. (rounded off to two decimal places)
Note: 1G=109
questions.explanationEn: Non-pipelined time per instruction = 5 / 1.6 ns = 3.125 ns. Pipelined CPI = 1 + 0.30 * 2 = 1.6, so pipelined time per instruction = 1.6 / 1.2 ns = 1.3333 ns. Speedup = 3.125 / (1.6 / 1.2) = (5 * 1.2) / (1.6 * 1.6) = 6 / 2.56 = 2.34375 (within 2.30 to 2.40).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a new TCP connection between a sender and a receiver. The receiver
advertised window is constant at 48 KB, the maximum segment size (MSS) is
2 KB, and the slow start threshold for TCP congestion control is 16 KB. Assume
that there are no timeouts or duplicate acknowledgements. The number of rounds
of transmission required for the congestion control algorithm of the TCP connection
to reach the congestion avoidance phase is ___________. (answer in integer)
Note: 1K=210
questions.explanationEn: With MSS = 2 KB and ssthresh = 16 KB = 8 MSS, slow start begins at cwnd = 1 MSS (Round 1 sends 1 MSS, cwnd becomes 2), Round 2 sends 2 MSS (cwnd becomes 4), Round 3 sends 4 MSS (cwnd becomes 8 = ssthresh), and the connection enters congestion avoidance on the 4th round of transmission.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the digital circuit shown below with two input lines A and B, two select
lines S0 and S1, and an output line Y. The blocks Q and M represent active high
2:4 decoder and 4-to-1 multiplexer, respectively. Out of 16 possible input
combinations, the number of combinations that produce Y=1 is ____________.
(answer in integer)
Note: One input combination is an instance of [A B S1 S0].
questions.explanationEn: In the 2:4 decoder (Q) feeding the 4:1 MUX (M), each combination of (A, B) activates exactly one decoder output line and each combination of (S1, S0) selects one MUX input line (refer to the official circuit wiring). Counting how many of the 16 input combinations [A B S1 S0] route a high (1) signal to Y gives 6 combinations.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.explanationEn: Let L = end + 1 - start. If L % 3 == 1 (L >= 1), func returns 1 + func(start, end-1) where the new length L-1 satisfies (L-1) % 3 == 0. From any L % 3 == 0, it transitions to L-1 (mod 3 == 2), and from L % 3 == 2 it transitions to L-2 (mod 3 == 0), alternating between 0 and 2 until L < 1 without ever hitting 1 mod 3 again. Thus 1 can be added at most once, making the maximum return value 1.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
The determinant of a 4 × 4 matrix A is 3. The value of the determinant of 2A is
____________. (answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: For any n x n matrix A and scalar k, det(kA) = k^n * det(A). Here n = 4, k = 2, and det(A) = 3, so det(2A) = 2^4 * 3 = 16 * 3 = 48.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Suppose an unbiased coin is tossed 6 times. Each coin toss is independent of all
previous coin tosses. Let E1 be the event that among the second, fourth, and sixth
coin tosses, there are at least two heads. Let E2 be the event that among the first,
second, third, and fifth coin tosses, there are equal number of heads and tails.
The conditional probability P(E1| E2) is equal to ____________. (rounded off to
one decimal place)
questions.explanationEn: Event E1 depends on tosses {2, 4, 6}, while E2 depends on tosses {1, 2, 3, 5}. Note that among tosses {1, 2, 3, 5}, by symmetry P(toss 2 = H | E2) = 1/2 (exactly half of the C(4, 2) = 6 outcomes of E2 have toss 2 = H), and tosses {4, 6} are completely independent of E2! Thus conditional on E2, tosses {2, 4, 6} are still independent fair coins, so P(E1 | E2) = P(at least 2 heads in 3 fair tosses) = (C(3,2) + C(3,3)) / 8 = 4 / 8 = 0.5.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a function f: (0,1) →{0, 1} defined as follows.
For a real number r∈(0,1) , f(r) = 1 if the second digit after the decimal point
in r is one of the four digits 2, 3, 6 and 7. Otherwise, f(r) is equal to 0.
The number of points in (0,1) at which f is discontinuous is ___________. (answer
in integer)
questions.explanationEn: In (0, 1), r = 0.d1 d2 ... has f(r) = 1 iff d2 in {2, 3, 6, 7}. For each of the 10 choices of the first digit d1 in {0..9}, f(r) equals 1 on the two intervals [0.d1 2, 0.d1 4) and [0.d1 6, 0.d1 8) (using standard non-terminating/terminating boundary transitions at 0.d1 2, 0.d1 4, 0.d1 6, and 0.d1 8). Each of these 4 points per d1 is a jump discontinuity of f, giving 10 * 4 = 40 discontinuities.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 2 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
It is necessary to design a link-layer protocol between two hosts that are directly
connected over a lossless link of length 3000 kilometers. Assume that the link
bandwidth is 108 bits per second and that the propagation delay in the link is 5
nanoseconds per meter. Every transmitted data byte is assigned a unique sequence
number.
Let N be the minimum number of bits needed for the sequence number field in the
protocol header such that
i.
the sequence numbers do not wrap around before 60 seconds, and
ii.
the maximum utilization of the link is achieved.
The value of N is ______. (answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: At 10^8 bps = 1.25 * 10^7 bytes/sec over 60 seconds, 60 * 1.25 * 10^7 = 7.5 * 10^8 bytes are transmitted, requiring ceil(log2(7.5 * 10^8)) = 30 bits to avoid sequence number wrap-around before 60 s. Meanwhile, RTT = 2 * 3 * 10^6 m * 5 ns/m = 30 ms, so bandwidth-delay product is 0.03 * 1.25 * 10^7 = 3.75 * 10^5 bytes (~19–20 bits), leaving N = 30 bits.
